record.context_brief: separating cycles with face-width at least three
record.original_question: Does every graph embedded in an orientable surface of genus at least 2 and face-width at least 3 contain a non-contractible cycle that separates the surface?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.4 Every graph embedded on an orientable surface of genus at least 2 with face-width at least 3 contains a non-contractible surface-separating cycle.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $G$ be a graph 2-cell embedded in $\Sigma$. The face-width (representativity) of the embedding is the minimum number of intersection points of $G$ with any non-contractible simple closed curve in $\Sigma$. A cycle $C$ of $G$ is called non-contractible if, viewed as a simple closed curve in $\Sigma$, it is not homotopic to a point, and is called surface-separating if $\Sigma \setminus C$ is disconnected.

Prove or disprove: every graph $G$ embedded in a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$ with face-width at least $3$ contains a non-contractible surface-separating cycle.
artifact.category_tag: Topological graph theory / graph embeddings on surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Zha, 1991) is known to remain open. Partial results establish it for larger face-width: Richter–Vitray proved it for face-width at least 11, and Zha–Zhao and Brunet–Mohar–Richter improved this to face-width 6 (and 5 in the nonorientable case). The face-width 3 case appears unresolved as of Mohar's open problem list.

status_evidence.title: Problems from the book Graphs on Surfaces (Mohar)
status_evidence.snippet: Zha's conjecture: every graph embedded in surface of genus ≥2 with face-width ≥3 contains a noncontractible surface separating cycle; proven for face-width ≥6 (Zha-Zhao; Brunet-Mohar-Richter), ≥11 (Richter-Vitray).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture for face-width 3 remains open; only weakened versions with larger face-width have been proved.
